title: Affine open refinement of a prescribed atlas and its scheme-test pullbacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. All schemes are over $S$ in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $|E|$ for its field-valued point classes and $|t|:|T|\to|E|$ for the map of a scheme-source morphism, as in [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. Let $p:h_V\to E$ be representable surjective etale and let $(U_i\subseteq V)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed open covering [def-weil-open-immersion], without an affineness assumption. Form the scheme coproduct $W=\coprod_iU_i$ with its disjoint open components [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], let $r:W\to V$ be induced by the inclusions, and let $w=p\circ h_r$. For every scheme $T$ and $t:h_T\to E$, put $P=T\times_EV$ and $P_i=P\times_VU_i$ (sheaf fibre products, represented by schemes). The canonical morphism $\coprod_iP_i\to T\times_EW$ is an isomorphism of sheaves, so the right side is represented by this scheme coproduct. Each $P_i\to P$ is an open immersion, the $P_i$ cover $P$, and the projection $\coprod_iP_i\to T$ is surjective etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Consequently $w$ is representable surjective etale and $|w|$ is surjective. These assertions include the empty covering of the empty atlas. Moreover, for every such prescribed atlas $p$, there exists such a family $(U_i)$ with each $U_i$ affine (isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]) and with an affine open $S_i\subseteq S$ and a factorization $U_i\to S_i\to S$ of its structural morphism for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines), proof: the prescribed open covering, coproduct, and composite; expanded scheme-test pullback and residue-field point argument. The affine refinement and affine-base factorization are the first two sentences of the same proof, using the affine-open basis twice.

proof.text: For a scheme test t:h_T→E, use [def-trf-algebraic-space] to choose a representing square h_P→h_V over h_T→E. The étale and surjective scheme-test hypotheses give alternative representing squares; their unique pullback isomorphisms, reflected by Yoneda to schemes over S, transport étaleness and surjectivity to the chosen projection q:P→T. Write a:P→V for the other projection, obtained by the fully faithful Yoneda embedding.

source.place: Tag 03FX, representable-transformation composition expanded by uniqueness of representing pullbacks.

proof.text: Prove the coproduct comparison first entirely in schemes over S. Set W=∐U_i, r=Sigma.desc j, Q=P×_V W, and D_i=P×_V U_i using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pullback pasting makes the canonical l_i:D_i→Q the base change of U_i→W. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] these inclusions are open and disjoint, and by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] so are the l_i. For x in Q, choose a component U_i containing its image in W, and lift the compatible pair of points to D_i by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-pullback-compatible-point]. Thus the l_i cover Q. Mathlib nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of identifies this disjoint open cover as a scheme coproduct. The forgetful functor Over S→Scheme preserves coproducts and reflects isomorphisms, so the actual canonical map Sigma.desc l:∐D_i→Q is an isomorphism. This proves the square with projections Sigma.desc(pullback.snd≫Sigma.ι) and Sigma.desc(pullback.fst), and bottom maps r and a, is cartesian in Over S. Apply Yoneda and paste with the square of step 1. Coproduct uniqueness identifies the second projection after composition with q with exactly Sigma.desc(pullback.fst≫q), giving the prescribed presheaf pullback square. No section of E is glued.

source.place: Tag 03FX, scheme-test expansion of the coproduct refinement; Schemes Tags 01JY and 01JT for the pullback open immersions and point lifting.

proof.text: The projections D_i→P are open immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Given x in P, choose y in some U_i with j_i(y)=a(x); [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-pullback-compatible-point] gives a point in D_i mapping to x. Thus these opens cover P. Their composites with q are étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] makes their coproduct projection étale. For surjectivity, lift a point of T to P using q, then to D_i by the preceding covering argument, and then include it in ∐D_i. The squares of step 2 with these projection properties give all three refined scheme-test predicates in [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 03FX, representable surjective étaleness verified on scheme tests; Morphisms Tags 02GP, 02GN and 02GJ.

proof.text: For any presheaf F, any scheme-source morphism b:h_W→F which satisfies IsSurjective induces a surjection on point classes. Prove first that schemePointMap respects composition by a scheme morphism: the induced residue-field map and its naturality square give precisely the common-field relation of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], using [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. For a point class choose a representative e over Spec K, convert it to h_(Spec K)→F by Yoneda, and take its representing surjective test C→Spec K. The field spectrum has a point, so C has a point z. Its residue-field morphism gives a representative over κ(z); the cartesian equality identifies its image under b with the restriction of e. The common-extension relation therefore identifies the original point class with the image of z under C→W. Apply this to the refined atlas of step 3. No K-rational lift is assumed.

source.place: Tags 03BU and 03BV, together with Schemes Tag 01J9; the residue-field naturality argument for a surjective representable map.

proof.text: For each point x of V use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to choose an affine base open B_x containing its structural image. Apply the same basis theorem on V to choose an affine open A_x containing x inside the inverse image of B_x. Define U_x as the actual open subscheme A_x with structural morphism A_x→V→S, and define j_x to be its inclusion into V. The family covers V by the chosen memberships. The morphism V.hom.resLE gives U_x→B_x with composite equal to its structural map, as in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. The index is V itself, in the universe required by [def-weil-size-convention]. All preceding arguments quantify over arbitrary small index types and use covering points only when a point is given, so they also apply to empty atlases and empty coverings.

source.place: Tag 03FX, first two sentences of the proof; Schemes Tags 01IT and 01HI.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03FX, with the scheme coproduct pullback comparison proved using disjoint open components, scheme pullback point lifting (01JT) and pullback pasting. split_report.summary: Proved the prescribed-atlas refinement directly using existing DAG nodes only. The coproduct comparison is constructed on arbitrary scheme tests by clopen component decompositions, fibre-product uniqueness and morphism gluing; etaleness is source-local, and point surjectivity uses field extension and residue-field factorization. The affine-base refinement uses the affine-open basis twice. Statement and statement dependencies are unchanged; no new nodes or Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the 03FX open-refinement input below lem-a1-affine-hc0 through the existing proetale-local-system representability and fpqc descent route. Retains the prescribed-atlas scheme-test construction extracted from parent lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover, and its affine-base refinement, without invoking that parent.

tool_uses.why: Uses only the general definition of representable surjective etale maps by scheme tests, with no trace-formula hypotheses or alternate proof route.
Uses the generic inclusion of Zariski coverings in the big fppf topology to check equality of sections of E on the disjoint open components; the unit supplies no replacement for this topology tool.

Steps: (1) open-fibre-product with base V, X=P and Y=V identifies P_i with q^{-1}(U_i), so the P_i cover P. The two composites C→E agree on C because E is an fppf sheaf and the Zariski cover by components is fppf. (4) Points: Spec-field factorization gives agreement over the common field κ(z), compatibly over S, with no rational lift assumed. (5) The affine basis is applied twice and open factorization gives U_v→S_v→S, indexed by the points of V. lean.statement: theorem space_atlas_open_refinement_pullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (V : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj V ⟶ E.obj.obj) (hp : IsRepresentable p) (hpEt : IsEtale p) (hpSurj : IsSurjective p) : (∀ (I : Type v) [Small.{u} I] (U : I → Over S) (j : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ V), (∀ i : I, IsOpenImmersion (j i).left) → (∀ x : V.left, ∃ (i : I) (y : (U i).left), (j i).left y = x) → (∀ (T : Over S) (t : yoneda.obj T ⟶ E.obj.obj), ∃ (P : Over S) (q : P ⟶ T) (a : P ⟶ V), IsPullback (yoneda.map a) (yoneda.map q) p t ∧ (∀ i : I, IsOpenImmersion (pullback.fst a (j i)).left) ∧ (∀ x : P.left, ∃ (i : I) (y : (Limits.pullback a (j i)).left), (pullback.fst a (j i)).left y = x) ∧ IsPullback (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ pullback.snd a (j i) ≫ Sigma.ι U i))) (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ pullback.fst a (j i) ≫ q))) (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc j) ≫ p) t ∧ Surjective (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ pullback.fst a (j i) ≫ q)).left ∧ Etale (Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ pullback.fst a (j i) ≫ q)).left) ∧ IsRepresentable (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc j) ≫ p) ∧ IsSurjective (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc j) ≫ p) ∧ IsEtale (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc j) ≫ p) ∧ Function.Surjective (schemePointMap (yoneda.map (Sigma.desc j) ≫ p))) ∧ ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Over S) (j : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ V), (∀ i : I, IsOpenImmersion (j i).left) ∧ (∀ x : V.left, ∃ (i : I) (y : (U i).left), (j i).left y = x) ∧ (∀ i : I, IsAffine (U i).left) ∧ (∀ i : I, ∃ (B : S.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen B) (b : (U i).left ⟶ B.toScheme), b ≫ B.ι = (U i).hom)
